target.title: fix(auth): use sanitized profile name for Codex import even without id- prefix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a profile name collision bug when importing OpenAI Codex auth credentials that lack an explicit `accountId`. Previously, the helper function `resolveOpenAICodexImportProfileName` would only accept the `profileName` if it started with the `id-` prefix; otherwise, it fell back to a hardcoded string parameter (e.g., `codex-import`). If multiple accounts lacking an `accountId` but having different profile names (like email addresses) were imported, they would all fall back to the same name, colliding and overwriting each other.

## Why This Change Was Made

Updated `resolveOpenAICodexImportProfileName` in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.ts` to accept the `profileName` regardless of prefix, after sanitizing it to remove illegal characters (such as `@`).

## User Impact

Prevents credential import collisions when migrating multiple Codex auth profiles that lack explicit account IDs but have distinct profile names.

## Evidence

Passed unit tests on branch `fix/1.5-codex-import-profile-name-collision` in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.test.ts`:
```
 ✓ |unit-fast| src/plugin-sdk/provider-openai-chatgpt-auth.test.ts (5 tests) 4ms
```

### Real Behavior Proof

Verified that email-based profile names (e.g. `peter@example.com`) are correctly sanitized to `peter-example.com` instead of falling back to `codex-import`:
```
resolveOpenAICodexImportProfileName({ profileName: "peter@example.com" }, "codex-import")
// Returns: "peter-example.com"
```
